Services and timers

Every systemd service, timer and path unit SATOM installs — what it runs, when, under which account and on which node of a pair — and how to check them.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer side — /etc/systemd/system/satom*.{service,timer,path}; templates in /opt/satom/deploy/

  • satom-alerts.timer — alert engine

  • satom-responder.timer — Sentinel response runner

Overview#

A SATOM node runs one web service and several small helpers. All of them share the code in /opt/satom and read /opt/satom/.env. The unit templates ship in /opt/satom/deploy/; the installer copies them to /etc/systemd/system/ and adds drop-ins for the service account.

Unit Type When it runs Account HA role
satom.service long-running always service account both nodes
satom-scheduler.service long-running always (fires only on primary) service account primary fires, standby waits
satom-reconciler.service long-running tick every 60 s service account both nodes
satom-metrics.service long-running always service account both nodes (own data each)
satom-alerts.timer → .service oneshot every 15 min service account both; notifications only on primary
satom-cert-renew.timer → .service oneshot daily 03:30 (+ up to 30 min) service account both nodes
satom-responder.timer → .service oneshot every 60 s service account both nodes
satom-integrations.path → .service oneshot when a hook request is queued service account both nodes
satom-updater.path → .service oneshot when an update/privileged request is queued root both nodes
satom-ha-datasync.timer → .service oneshot every 5 min service account cluster installs only; acts only on the standby

"Service account" means the account pinned by the installer drop-in (satom unless SATOM_APP_USER was set at install time).

❗Important — The templates say User=root — the drop-in is what counts

satom.service, satom-scheduler.service and satom-reconciler.service in deploy/ declare User=root, and the alerts, cert-renew and updater templates declare no user. The installer rewrites User= in the installed copies and writes /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/10-app-user.conf for every shipped deploy/*.service except satom-updater.service (plus the generated satom-ha-datasync.service), because every software update copies the templates again; the self-update runner rewrites the same drop-ins on each update. satom-updater.service is the only unit meant to run as root. Check the effective account with systemctl show -p User <unit>.

Long-running services#

satom.service — web application#

  • Runs: gunicorn --workers 4 --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --timeout 600 with access and error logs in /var/log/satom/access.log and /var/log/satom/error.log.
  • Bind: the shipped unit listens on loopback only, so only nginx reaches it; a software update no longer re-opens 0.0.0.0:8000.
  • Restart: Restart=always, 5 s delay.
  • Restart it after any Python or template change; static JS/CSS do not need a restart.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the shipped satom.service binds gunicorn to 127.0.0.1:8000 (existing nodes receive the corrected unit at their next update), and with a custom SATOM_APP_USER the installer now pins every service, including the integration hook runner, to that account at install time.

satom-scheduler.service — scheduled actions#

  • Runs: deploy/scheduler_guard.sh, which loops on deploy/satom-node-role.sh. When the local PostgreSQL answers "primary" it execs python -m app.scheduler_runtime; otherwise it sleeps 30 s and asks again. A promotion therefore starts the scheduler with no extra step.
  • What it does: every 45 s it releases stale leases, then claims due scheduled actions and runs each one once. Overdue actions without catch-up are moved to their next run and marked missed. Wall-clock schedules use the time zone configured in Settings.
  • Why separate: the four web workers would otherwise fire every action four times.

satom-reconciler.service — code reconciler#

  • Runs: python -m app.reconciler_runtime, ticking every 60 s; Restart=always, 15 s delay.
  • What it does: compares this node's code with the expected revision. In MANUAL mode (default) it only records the drift. In AUTO mode it drives the staged self-update: standby first, then the primary, health-gated. It does not boot the Flask application, so it runs on the read-only standby too. Its status is shown on the Software update and High availability pages.

satom-metrics.service — metrics store#

  • Runs: /usr/local/bin/victoria-metrics with -storageDataPath=/var/lib/satom-metrics, -httpListenAddr=127.0.0.1:8428, -retentionPeriod=396d, -memory.allowedBytes=512MiB, -search.maxQueryDuration=30s.
  • Installed and enabled only if the binary is present (the installer places it from the offline bundle or downloads the pinned release). Each node keeps its own store; it is not replicated. See Metrics.

Timers#

satom-alerts.timer — alert engine#

  • Schedule: OnCalendar=*:0/15 (every 15 minutes), 3 min after boot, randomised by up to 60 s, Persistent=true.
  • Runs: deploy/satom-alerts.sh → flask alerts-run, which evaluates the proactive checks (certificates, device reachability, git lag, backups…) and dispatches new alerts by e-mail and the in-app bell. See Alerting.
  • On a standby: findings are evaluated and sent to syslog, but in-app notifications and e-mail are skipped ("read-only replica — notification is primary-only"). A promoted standby starts dispatching automatically.
  • Exit status: a run that found new alerts but reached no channel exits non-zero, so the unit shows failed. If the run itself crashes (for example because the database is down), the script writes disk, memory and load figures to the journal and to syslog.

satom-cert-renew.timer — node certificate#

  • Schedule: daily at 03:30, randomised by up to 30 min, Persistent=true.
  • Runs: deploy/satom-cert-renew.sh → flask cert-renew. Renews the node's service certificate when it was issued by the internal CA and is within the renewal threshold; does nothing for imported or bootstrap certificates. If the renewal mode is autopull, it also fetches the renewed certificate from the configured source. Every run is recorded in the renewal journal. See Node TLS.

satom-responder.timer — Sentinel response runner#

  • Schedule: every 60 s (OnUnitActiveSec=60s), 90 s after boot.
  • Runs: python -m app.cli_sentinel responder-tick as the service account, with a 300 s start timeout.
  • What it does: executes queued Sentinel response actions and expires blocks whose time-to-live has passed. Gates are re-evaluated at execution time. The timer is enabled even though the response engine ships disarmed, because it is also what lifts expired blocks. See Sentinel.

satom-ha-datasync.timer — data/ sync (cluster only)#

  • Written by the installer only in cluster mode: 2 min after boot, then every 5 min.
  • Runs: deploy/satom-ha-datasync.sh. Exits immediately unless this node's PostgreSQL is a standby and the HA mode is not standalone. Finds the peer in data/ha_nodes.json and pulls the primary's data/ with rsync -az --delete over SSH (key /opt/satom/.ssh/id_ha_rsync, strict host key checking), excluding jobs/, tmp/, update-requests/, update-status/, logs/, diagnostics/ and deep_jobs/.

Path-activated units#

satom-updater.path → satom-updater.service (root)#

  • Trigger: DirectoryNotEmpty=/opt/satom/data/update-requests.
  • Runs: the privileged update runner self_update_runner.py (start timeout 1800 s). The installer redirects ExecStart through a drop-in to a root-owned copy in /usr/local/lib/satom-runner/ using a system Python, so the service account cannot alter what root executes.
  • What it does: code update (git), pip install, flask db upgrade, refreshed unit files and service restarts, with automatic rollback when the post-restart health check (/healthz, 90 s) fails. It also carries the other root-only requests (for example an nginx reload, the PostgreSQL TLS protocol and cipher settings from Node TLS, or a standby promotion). Status is written to data/update-status/. See Software update and Offline updates.

⚠️Warning — Must be enabled on both nodes

A node whose satom-updater.path (or satom-integrations.path) is disabled accepts queued requests and never runs them.

satom-integrations.path → satom-integrations.service#

  • Trigger: DirectoryNotEmpty=/opt/satom/data/integrations/queue.
  • Runs: python -m app.services.hook_runner as the service account, 900 s timeout, with extra hardening (ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, NoNewPrivileges, write access only to data/integrations).
  • What it does: runs integration hooks in a child process that cannot import the application, does not inherit its environment and receives only the secrets the hook declared. A timeout kills the whole process group. See Integrations.

Checking the units#

systemctl list-units 'satom*' --all
systemctl list-timers 'satom*'
systemctl status satom.service
journalctl -u satom-scheduler.service -n 100 --no-pager
journalctl -u satom-alerts.service --since today
tail -f /var/log/satom/error.log

The operator CLI wraps the same checks:

sudo satom diagnose units        # inventory and privilege drop-ins
sudo satom diagnose scheduler    # is anything automated actually firing here?
sudo satom diagnose service scheduler
sudo satom execute restart web   # waits for /healthz to answer 200

The CLI uses short aliases: web, scheduler, reconciler, updater, alerts, cert-renew, metrics, responder, datasync, nginx, postgres. execute restart|start|stop accepts only web, scheduler, reconciler, alerts, cert-renew, metrics, datasync and nginx — the privileged updater and postgres are refused on purpose. See CLI.

Advanced Which node runs what, and how it knows

All role decisions use SELECT pg_is_in_recovery() with the application's own database credentials (deploy/satom-node-role.sh prints f for primary or standalone, t for standby). The installer enables every unit on both nodes; the scheduler guard, the alert engine and the data sync check the role themselves, so after a promotion the new primary is already set up.

Advanced Retired units

satom-git-publish.timer is no longer installed: the device source of truth is versioned locally (see Data and storage).

#systemd#service#timer#path unit#scheduler#reconciler#alerts#cert renew#responder#integrations#updater#metrics#datasync#journalctl
